Siloxanes are silicon-containing organic compounds with Si-O-Si linkages. Most siloxanes, especially the volatile methyl siloxanes (VMS) like hexamethyldisiloxane and octamethylcyclotetrasiloxane, are known to be combustible liquids. They have flash points that classify them as combustible rather than highly flammable, though this can vary somewhat depending on the specific siloxane compound.

Siloxanes are not flame-retardant (they don't inhibit flames) and they are not non-flammable (they will burn under the right conditions). However, they are generally less flammable than many hydrocarbons, falling into the combustible category.
